answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a slashable bond that unlocks only after a stretch of graded, useful work. One honest agent pays that cost once. An attacker spinning up a spiral of a thousand fake accounts, each flying a violet flag, must lock a thousand separate bonds — and when the gale of peer review exposes them as copies, every bond is burned. Faking scale ends up costing far more than earning trust.
